CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center

PATIENT: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
SPECIMEN TYPE: Placental tissue
COLLECTION DATE: [redacted date]
REPORT DATE: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Prenatal testing of fetal tissue

TEST PERFORMED
Array Comparative Genomic Hybridization (Array CGH)
Quantitative Fluorescence-Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR)

METHODOLOGY
Array CGH: Oligonucleotide array analysis performed using GeneScan HR60 platform containing approximately 60,000 genome-wide probes with 120kb median resolution. DNA extracted from placental tissue and hybridized according to manufacturer's protocol. Data analysis performed using GenomeView software with GRCh37/hg19 reference genome.

QF-PCR: Multiplex QF-PCR analysis for rapid aneuploidy detection and triploidy screening.

RESULTS

ARRAY CGH RESULT: arr(1-22)x2,(X,Y)x1
Normal male chromosome complement
No copy number imbalances detected

QF-PCR RESULT: Normal male pattern
No evidence of triploidy
No evidence of common aneuploidies (13, 18, 21, X, Y)

INTERPRETATION
Array CGH analysis reveals a normal male chromosomal complement with no detectable copy number imbalances. The resolution of this array excludes chromosomal imbalances greater than 3Mb of known fully penetrant pathogenicity. Smaller imbalances, balanced rearrangements, low-level mosaicism (<20%), and single gene mutations are not excluded by this analysis.

QF-PCR results are consistent with a normal male karyotype with no evidence of triploidy or common aneuploidies.

RECOMMENDATIONS
No further chromosome analysis is required based on these results.

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted location] Cytogenetics Laboratory. The laboratory is certified under Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) to perform high-complexity testing.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
